title: Dimension-zero normalization of a supplied finite smooth orientation
statement: For the supplied geometrically normalized orientation of finite smooth purity, in relative dimension zero the actual tensor mate composed with the supplied graph-normalized etale adjoint coordinates equals zeroSourceMap. The maps are exactly those of [def-pur-finite-smooth-canonical-maps] and [def-pur-finite-smooth-adjunction-data]. This is solely the geometric normalization step: naturality, constructible domains, actual origin counits, trace transport and the deduction of the dimension-zero trace equation are proved in the level assembly.

source.place: sk-thm-smooth-purity and proof: inverse diagonal orientation followed by the tensor map; sk-prop-sp-orientation.proof.md: diagonal, deformation, vector bundle; sk-lem-sp-reduction.proof.md and sk-lem-sp-reduction-compatibilities.proof.md: counit-defined coefficient comparisons and quotient cocycle. The ordinary-etale Noetherian formulation retains arbitrary ground fields.

proof.text: First transport finite smooth gamma normalization from its single universe lift of Z/(ell^n) to the double lift used here, along the canonical ring equivalence. Extension and restriction along that equivalence preserve the units, root generators, tensor products and adjunction counits; the normalized comparisons identify the actual arrows. Apply finite smooth gamma normalization for the supplied graph-normalized sum comparison. The supplied section specialization and its comparison restrict to identity at one, so uniqueness of normalized section specialization identifies the deformation factors. In relative dimension zero the diagonal normal bundle has rank zero. Under its canonical cone-to-bundle identification, rank-zero bundle integration and the unit identification give the same rank-zero factor as finite smooth gamma normalization. Substitution in OrientationNormalized identifies alpha with its normalized omega coordinates. The tensor mate identity then gives the required equation, with the empty tensor identified using zeroLineIso.

lean.statement:
theorem finiteSmoothIntrinsicLevelProperties
    (ell : ℕ) [Fact ell.Prime]
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] [IsNoetherian Y]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [HasCompactification f] [QuasiCompact f] [IsSeparated f]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (d : ℕ) [SmoothOfRelativeDimension d f]
    (hY : ∀ y : Y, IsUnit (ell : Y.presheaf.stalk y))
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n)
    (G : FiniteRingSectionDeformation.Geometry d
      (pullback.fst f f) (pullback.diagonal f))
    (hX : IsUnit ((ell ^ n : ℕ) : Γ(X, ⊤)))
    (alpha : dualizingComplex (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (coefficient ell n)) f ≅
      line (coefficient ell n) (ell ^ n) (CharP.cast_eq_zero _ _) X d)
    (hAlpha : OrientationNormalized (coefficient ell n) (ell ^ n)
      (pow_pos (Fact.out : ell.Prime).pos n) (CharP.cast_eq_zero _ _) f d G hX alpha) :
    let A := coefficient ell n;
    let N := ell ^ n;
    let hA : (N : A) = 0 := CharP.cast_eq_zero _ _;
    /- dimension_zero -/
    (∀ hd : d = 0, ∀ [Etale f],
      ∀ C : FiniteSmoothCompactSupportComparisons A, FiniteSmoothComparisonNormalized A C →
      ∀ K : DerivedCategoryModule A Y,
        gamma A f (line A N hA X d) alpha K ≫
            (finiteSmoothAdjointCoordinates A C f).hom.app K = zeroSourceMap A N hA f d hd K)
